correctness.rationale: The exact definition is equivalent to existence of a symmetric word-period. For weight three the three possible numbers of root markers yield a complete dichotomy: symmetric full word when two cyclic gaps coincide; otherwise intervals I_g and I_0 exhaust proper symmetric word-periods. The resulting C(u,v,h) formula is proved by interval inclusion; the generating function follows from a disjoint equal-gap/distinct-gap partition and exact finite geometric identities. Algebraic reduction and partial fractions give the quasipolynomial and 1/3 density. The actual standalone verifier checked 7,315 individual words at lengths 3..21, an independent direct length count, and exact rational recurrence vs gap sums through length 160. No finite test is substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Statement/implication comparisons: Simpson (2024) introduces palindromic periodicities and studies structural periodicity; Fici--Shallit--Simpson (2024 preprint, 2025 full HTML) prove inclusions and automatic-word factor results and explicitly leave total binary enumeration asymptotics open. Neither inspected text provides fixed-weight-three gap counts, generating function, or density. Guo--Shallit--Shur (2015) enumerates the smaller class of products of two palindromes: word 01100100 is a palindromic periodicity but is not symmetric, proving that result cannot imply this count alone. OEIS A374495 counts all Hamming weights, not this slice. Literature searches and statement comparisons found no dominating fixed-weight-three result. Residual unindexed equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed synonymous formula for a fixed three-marker/palindrome-period composition could predate this claim despite no retrieved match.
Historical symmetric-word enumeration (including Kemp 1982) has a strict-subclass object; a separately unpublished extension of its methods cannot be ruled out.
The original 2024 Simpson treatment uses auxiliary conditions in parts of its presentation; the current count explicitly follows the subsequently standardized symmetric-word-period definition.

value.rationale: This is the first Hamming-weight layer in which palindromic periodicity is nonautomatic: all words of weight at most two are symmetric. It gives a complete all-length sparse-sector classification with a nontrivial rational generating function and one-third limiting density. The primary literature explicitly leaves unrestricted binary enumeration asymptotics as an open question; a natural exact fixed-content slice is mathematically informative even without settling that larger problem. The nontrapezoidal/nonsymmetric example shows the result is not a routine specialization of earlier sufficient-class theorems.
